priceSnapshot.note: Midday's reduce line held. The session low since the 18:00Z mark is 63,309.4, printed on the 19:00Z hourly bar, which is 71.8 points above the 63,237.6 trigger midday published and 105.4 points above the 63,204 area where the shelf thinned out. Price never settled a single 1H bar below the line, so reduce_fired is false and the two-day low remains intact for a third session. From that low the tape has built a six-hour base and is now leaving the top of it: the 20:00Z hourly closed 63,599.9 on a 177-point range, the 23:00Z hourly closed 63,484.7, and the two most recent 15m bars printed 63,606.0 and then reached 63,716.9 - the highest trade since 18:00Z. Spot sits at 63,584.4 as this is written. The fast chart has genuinely turned: 15m RSI is 59.43, the 15m MACD histogram is +23.15 and expanding from the +3.80 midday flagged, and price is above both the 15m EMA20 at 63,501.26 and the EMA50 at 63,573.54. None of that repairs the damage one timeframe up. The 4H EMA200 sits at 63,724.31 and the last three settled 4H bars closed 63,445.9, 63,423.2 and 63,484.7 - all below it - with the 4H MACD histogram widening negative from -70.86, and 4H RSI at 38.94. The 1H EMA20 at 63,630.55 is still overhead and unreclaimed on a settled basis. So this is a bounce inside a broken structure, not a repair of it. The single most important thing that changed since midday is not on the price chart at all. July CPI came in a tenth cooler than June across headline, core and year-over-year, and US equities took it and ran: QQQ closed 723.70 (+0.73%), VOO 710.17 (+0.25%) and JPXN 104.71 (+1.27%), and all three closed at or within 0.1% of their 21-day highs. BTC spent that same session making a lower low. An asset that cannot rally on a cooler inflation print, on the day its risk-asset cousins print monthly highs, is telling you where the marginal bid is not.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close below $63,309.4 - the low of this session's six-hour base, printed on the 19:00Z bar. The line is raised from midday's 63,237.6 rather than left where it was, and the reason is that the base itself is now the structure worth defending: price has spent six hours building higher lows above 63,309.4 and the level has become the floor a long is actually leaning on. Losing it on a settle does not merely re-test the two-day low at 63,237.6, it removes the only thing that has held since 19:00Z, and the liquidation map underneath is thin - $177,233 at 63,300 and nothing meaningful again until 63,000 - so a break has very little to absorb it. The 63,400 bucket is the day's single largest at $627,657, but that is REALIZED mass, already consumed on the way down; it will not catch price a second time.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close above $63,900 with aggregate open interest NOT rising across the same bar. The price line is held at midday's number and it is unchanged for a reason: 63,900 is still the first level that puts price clear of the 4H EMA200 at 63,724.31 with room to spare, clears the 1H EMA20 at 63,630.55, and sits on top of the $329,783 shelf rather than beneath it. Anything short of that is a bounce inside a broken 4H, which is exactly what the last six hours have been. The open-interest condition matters more tonight than it has all week. Open interest has risen for a third consecutive read - $2,062,574,395 at the morning mark, $2,086,233,942 at midday, $2,120,231,576 now, +1.63% since midday - while the OKX long/short account ratio went 1.68, 1.83, 1.89. The crowd has added longs into every leg of this decline. A bounce funded by that same crowd is the one this filter exists to refuse.

decisionBox.changed: Stance stays REDUCE and the wallet trims a further 20% of the spot core, but the reasoning is the opposite of midday's. Midday trimmed because its own reduce line had fired with margin; this session trims because nothing fired and the setup got worse anyway. Midday's 63,237.6 line was never touched on a settle - a clean, correct hold - and yet across those six and a half hours open interest rose another 1.63% to $2,120,231,576, the long/short account ratio climbed 1.83 to 1.89, funding stayed positive at +0.01000% per 8h, and realized long liquidations ran $2,652,630 against $1,227,897 of shorts. Longs paid for the flush and then bought more. Set that against the price action - a bounce that has still not settled a 1H bar above the 63,630.55 EMA20, under a 4H EMA200 at 63,724.31 that has now rejected three consecutive settles - and against BTC failing to participate in a post-CPI session where QQQ, VOO and JPXN all closed at 21-day highs. The trim is 20% and not more because the honest read is genuinely two-sided: the 15m has turned up with the histogram at +23.15, the base is six hours old and making higher lows, and the downside cluster is thin enough that a flush would have little fuel. This is not a call for a crash. It is a call for less spot into a nine-hour overnight gap with no scheduled catalyst to resolve it, which takes the book from roughly 62% invested to roughly 50/50 and hands the midnight session a genuine choice instead of an inherited position. The resting stop stays at 63,190, below the 63,237.6 two-day low rather than inside the thin band above it. Futures stay flat for a third consecutive session - there is no leverage edge in a 407-point range.

overnightRisk: The gap to the next report is roughly nine hours - this desk publishes again at 02:00 COT / 07:00Z - and it spans the thinnest liquidity of the week: the US cash close is behind us, Asia opens into it, and there is no scheduled macro release in the window. The specific risk is not a headline, it is positioning. Open interest has risen 1.63% since midday to $2,120,231,576 while the OKX long/short account ratio pushed to 1.89, its highest read of the day, and funding held positive at +0.01000% per 8h. That is a book that got longer on every down-leg, and it is now leaning on a six-hour base whose floor is 63,309.4. Below that floor the realized-liquidation map is close to empty - $177,233 at 63,300 and no meaningful shelf again until the 63,000 handle - so if 63,309.4 gives way on a settle there is very little between price and 63,000 to slow it, and a crowded long book is exactly the fuel that turns a slow drift into a cascade. The mirror risk is real too and should not be dismissed: $2,868,394 of realized mass sits above spot across 63,600 to 64,400, and a short-squeeze reclaim of the 4H EMA200 at 63,724.31 would run into a genuine vacuum on the way up. That is the less likely path tonight - the crowd is long, not short, so there is less trapped fuel above than the raw cluster weight suggests - but it is why this session trims 20% rather than flattening. Two named catalysts to watch if the tape moves without an obvious cause: the 12 Aug US spot BTC ETF flow print, which Farside still shows as 0.0 because same-day totals are published after the US close and will land inside this gap after a +$7.8m day that was barely distinguishable from zero; and the 08:00Z funding settlement, where a further rise from +0.01000% would confirm the long crowd paid to stay long through the night. The resting stop at 63,190 is the only protection that works while nobody is watching, and it is placed deliberately below the 63,237.6 two-day low rather than inside the thin 63,300 band, so it measures price leaving the zone instead of price hunting it.

calibration.note: Midday published reduceIf 63,237.6 and addIf 63,900 and NEITHER fired. The session low since the 18:00Z mark is 63,309.4, so the reduce line was missed by 71.8 points and no 1H bar settled anywhere near it; the high is 63,716.9, so the add line was missed by 183.1 points. Both lines were placed correctly and both survived - that is the level-setting working. The TRADE is the part that did not. Midday trimmed 25% of the spot core at 63,445.0 and price now marks 63,584.4, so the trim is 139.4 points offside, roughly -0.22% on the trimmed notional, about -$0.07. So the honest verdict is the mirror of 11 August midday: process correct, outcome negative, magnitude trivial because the size was partial. The pattern worth naming is that this desk has now been wrong-footed in the same direction three sessions running - morning added into a CPI window and lost 1.23%, midday trimmed into a base and gave back 0.22%, and both were defensible ex ante. The common thread is acting AT the level rather than waiting for the level to resolve, and the rolling record shows it: 6 of the last 20 verdicts helped, against 36 of 73 all-time. That degradation is real and this session's response to it is to size the trim at 20% rather than 40%, and to place the stop below the structure rather than inside it.
